engagement_title: Redecker Machine Works mark recovery: rebuild the 1919 mark from a screened 1974 catalogue cover and a photographed nameplate, recover the struck works proving stamp and the cast 1919 heritage device beside it into one system of three marks, then carry them onto the November data plate run, the usage sheet and the stationery
vertical: Manufacturing and industrial capital equipment, press brakes and metal forming presses, a third generation family works in Sheboygan, Wisconsin selling to procurement engineers and plant managers across North America and northern Europe
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Freelancer.com logo brief carried in the ledger, which asks for the mark in 'fully editable vector format (.ai or .eps)', 'instantly readable at small sizes' on labels and swing tags, with 'print-ready CMYK output and scalable vector artwork', shipped with 'one-colour and reverse variants'. Designing a NEW mark from nothing is outside this connector, so the doable and honest reading of that requirement is the commission this client actually needed: take the artwork they still physically have, recover it as clean scalable production geometry, and ship the variants and production files the trades downstream require. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes the fuller version real, because an ink level trace off photographed printed collateral genuinely recovers a mark, a flat press PDF genuinely becomes a live merge template running one record per page, and HTML authoring genuinely produces a native editable document at true print canvases. The posting names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional works Redecker Machine Works. Absorbs AO-93.
client_one_liner: The only artwork left for our company mark is a scan of a 1974 catalogue cover and a photo of it etched into a machine nameplate, and fourteen machines ship in November that all need plates.
client_brief:
Redecker Machine Works, mark recovery and the November shipping season

We build press brakes and metal forming presses in Sheboygan, Wisconsin. Third generation, forty one people, machines from forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars. Our buyer is a procurement engineer or a plant manager who has read the tolerance sheet before he reads anything we wrote.

Here is the problem. The company mark has been on every machine since 1919 and we no longer have artwork for it in any usable form. The designer who last touched it retired in the nineties and nothing came back from his files. What we have is a flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, where the mark is printed in one deep ink on cream board, and a photograph one of our fitters took of the same mark etched into the stainless nameplate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. We need the mark back as artwork we can hand to anybody: our sign shop, our plate engraver, our printer, and the laser house that cuts the sign over the bay door.

It has to work everywhere. Big on the bay door sign. Small as a one colour stamp on an invoice. Reversed out of our works green on the machine plates. And it has to still be our mark. These customers buy precision from us, so if the mark on a two hundred thousand dollar machine looks soft it says something about the machine.

Two other marks go on the machines and we need those back too. Every machine gets our proving stamp struck into it once it has passed its load test, the little round one with the bend mark and a small box the inspector stamps the test number into, and the only copy of it is a photograph of it struck into a steel test offcut. And the old cast badge with the date on it, 1919, is raised into the main casting and painted over green, and it sits next to the name on the bay door sign. Our engraver needs the stamp as artwork he can cut a die from, and the sign shop needs the badge, and neither of them can work from a photograph.

Fourteen machines ship in November. Each needs its data plate: model, serial, year, voltage, phase, weight and the works address. Our printer has last year's plate artwork as a PDF and the fourteen machines are in a spreadsheet. We need the plates print ready and a proof of each we can sign off before they go to the engraver.

We also want a page showing the sign shop how much room to leave around the mark and which version goes where, plus a letterhead and a stamp we can edit ourselves later.

Tell us what you found and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine, bought by procurement engineers and plant managers on a specification rather than on a feeling. The band is load bearing in a way most identity work is not: at this price the mark is read as evidence about the machine, so a soft trace, a dotty edge or a designation that does not match the order book reads as tolerance drift on the shop floor and costs the quote. The correct register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, the works green used as a field rather than decoration. Push into heritage treatment, distressed texture or a hand drawn feel and it becomes a boutique metal shop selling five hundred dollar fire pits. Flatten it into consumer tech instead, thin geometric sans and pastels, and a procurement engineer stops believing there is a foundry behind it. Either extreme misreads the commission even if every file opens. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

Our buyer reads the tolerance sheet before he reads anything we wrote, so everything we put a name on has to say precision.
brand_identity.audience: Procurement engineers and plant managers who buy on specification rather than feeling, across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.price_positioning: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine. The mark is read as evidence about the machine: the register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, never heritage craft workshop and never consumer tech.
brand_identity.typography: A flat, mechanical grotesque for the mark and plate wording, set high contrast and widely spaced, paired with a plain industrial sans for the usage sheet and stationery. Nothing decorative, nothing hand drawn. Weight and spacing do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, factual and confident; we state the specification and let it stand. No adjectives a tolerance sheet would not carry. Example line the brand would write: "Built to a hundred years of the same standard, plate by plate."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We no longer hold usable artwork for the company mark in any form. The designer who last touched it retired in the nineties and nothing came back from his files. What survives is a flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, where the mark is printed in one deep ink on cream board, and a photograph a fitter took of the same mark etched into a stainless nameplate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. A works standards text file records the green as the paint shop mixes it, the address block and the required plate wording. Two further company marks also survive only as artefacts: the works proving stamp, held only as a die impression struck into a steel test coupon a fitter photographed, and the 1919 cast heritage device, held only as a raking light photograph of the badge cast and painted into a machine's main frame.
brand_identity.values: Precision as reputation: the mark on a two hundred thousand dollar machine has to be as true as the machine, reversed clean out of the works green, and unmistakably ours.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_catalogue_1974_cover.tif (4200 x 5600)
assets_supplied.kind: Flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, the mark printed large in one deep ink on cream board.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The 1974 parts catalogue. The mark is printed big on the cover, which is why we scanned it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: That cover was printed through a coarse screen, so at scan scale the ink edge is a field of dots rather than a line and a trace of it succeeds and returns lumpy stippled geometry that looks correct at canvas size. It also carries an outer arc of place type the nameplate version lacks, and the board is scanned off square.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_nameplate_rebuild.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the same mark etched into the brushed stainless nameplate of a rebuilt machine.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same mark, etched into the plate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. This is what it looks like on a machine today."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: There is no ink here at all: the mark is an etch in brushed stainless, so mark and ground sit at nearly the same value and a selection reads the brush grain as readily as the etch, biting the outer ring where the grain runs with it. Background removal on that ring returns a solid opaque disc rather than a knockout, and both results look plausible until the geometry is placed reversed on colour.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_proving_stamp_coupon.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Macro photograph of the works proving stamp struck by a hardened die into a polished steel test coupon, the small round acceptance mark every finished machine carries after its load test.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our proving stamp, struck into a test offcut. The inspector puts the test number in the little box. This is the only copy we have of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is struck metal with no ink, so the impression sits at nearly the value of the polished ground exactly as the nameplate does, but the die also raised a burnished burr right around the impression that reads as strongly as the struck line, so the isolation that takes the mark fattens it with the burr and the isolation that ducks the burr thins the ring rule and the number box away. The stamp only ever goes small, about nine millimetres struck into the plate corner, so a version that looks correct at coupon scale closes its bend angle apex and its ring counter into a blob at strike size, and the inspector's number box is empty in the die and must be recovered as an open knockout rather than a filled square. A faint offset ghost strike doubles some lines.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_frame_casting_1919.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Raking light photograph of the 1919 cast heritage badge raised into a machine's main frame casting and painted over in the works green, the secondary mark that sits beside the company mark on the bay door sign.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The old date badge, cast into the frame and painted green like the rest of the machine. It goes next to the name on the bay door sign."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The badge is cast in relief and then painted the works green over the raised iron, so it is green on green and the only thing separating it from the field is the directional shadow the relief throws under the raking shop light. A value or threshold selection therefore catches the cast shadow, which is offset from the true casting edge, and returns an emblem shifted and fattened toward the lit side, while the shallow draft angle on each raised stroke reads as a second edge so a naive trace double lines the strokes. The casting edge and the shadow edge both look like the mark until the result is set beside the company mark at bay door scale.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_plate_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's data plate artwork from the printer, a real press PDF, the plate centred on a US Letter page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file for last year's plates. The layout is right, only the machine details change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What a flat press file exposes as separately addressable blocks once it becomes a working layout is a property of how it was originally set rather than of how the printed plate looks, and the readout of its text can omit a whole run while keeping the line break around it, so every position past the omission is short by exactly what was dropped and the check still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_machines_november.csv (14 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The November order book: model, serial, build year, voltage, phase, shipping weight and a note column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The fourteen machines shipping in November, straight out of our order book."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One machine is a special build whose model designation carries a long suffix, and the plate's model line is a fixed frame that does not spill when it is overrun, it simply stops drawing, so that page comes back looking finished with the designation cut at the frame edge and nothing reports it. Two rows also carry the same serial because a machine was re entered when its order was split.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_works_standards.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the works green as the paint shop mixes it, the address block, and the required plate wording.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The green as our paint shop mixes it, our address, and the wording our plates have to carry."

acceptance_bar: The master mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, and counters and hairline rule still open at the sizes it actually reproduces.
The delivered geometry reads as OUR mark set beside both surviving sources. A redrawing fails. A soft or dotty edge fails even though the file opens and scales.

Three distinct marks are recovered as placeable geometry, not one mark plus decorations lifted off it: the company mark, the works proving stamp and the 1919 cast heritage device, each with its own viewBox and none a rescaled copy of another.

The proving stamp survives at the size it is actually struck. Its bend angle apex and ring counter stay open at about nine millimetres and the inspector's number box knocks out rather than filling, judged reversed on the works green rather than at coupon scale. A burr fattened blob fails.

The 1919 cast device is recovered from the casting edge rather than the raking light shadow, sits as a secondary mark beside the company mark without the outer place arc, and shows no doubled strokes from the cast draft.
One master, one family of variants. The one colour, reversed knockout and full colour versions are the same geometry, not three traces that have drifted apart.
The reversed variant genuinely knocks out on the works green, including the enclosed interior of the ring. A filled disc on green fails.
The laser file is a followable closed path system with no stray full canvas rectangle and no hairline that closes at cut scale.

The plate run is one print ready file carrying exactly one machine per page, fourteen pages in order, plus a sign off proof of each machine at true plate resolution carrying the machine it claims to carry.
Every field the works standards require is fully present at trim on every plate. A plate that looks finished but has lost the tail of a designation fails.
No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and every resize any tool performed is recorded rather than absorbed.

The usage sheet and stationery arrive as ONE working document we can edit, with the mark as live vector, text we can retype, and the clear space guidance drawn on the page as visible rules rather than described in a sentence.
One type system across the sheet and the stationery, named by family, by foundry or designer, and by the weight actually used.
The note tells us what could not be done as asked and why, including anything about the plate file our printer needs to hear from us.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, with image_vectorize counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface

adobe_surfaces.role: The whole recovery of all three marks. It isolates the company mark at ink level off a screened printed cover and at etch level off brushed stainless, opposite problems in the same shape, then recovers the two further marks in their own media, the proving stamp struck into steel and the heritage device cast and painted into iron, four physical media across three marks. For each it prepares the raster so the trace receives an edge rather than a texture, judges the result at the size that mark actually reproduces, and performs the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, pdf and x-indesign), document_render_layout (resolution, createSeparateFiles)

It reverse engineers the printer's flat press PDF into a live merge template, computing every text position against the document's own reconstructed story and confirming placeholders after the build rather than trusting a success message.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, upload every asset against its role, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen machines at one record per page is a merge run; the usage sheet and stationery are designed one offs needing an authored canvas. Choosing the wrong home for either loses the job before any craft happens.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview both company mark sources, the proving stamp coupon, the cast frame photograph and the printer's plate file, triage what medium each mark is in, how mark and ground separate on each and what the two company mark lockups differ by, then straighten what is off square.
trajectory.judgement: The client hands over what looks like pictures of marks. They are four physical objects in different media, ink pressed into board, an etch cut out of brushed metal, a die struck into a coupon and a badge cast and painted into iron, which do not respond to the same treatment, and one company mark source may not be recoverable at all. Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: A per source triage note across all four mark photographs and levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Isolate the mark on the catalogue cover by naming the ink's own visual properties rather than the object it is printed on, set the polarity the trace needs, and crop to the isolation's own returned extent.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the board and returns a card shaped blob every later step processes as if it were the mark. Polarity is the difference between a positive mark and a black box, and both report success.
trajectory.produces: A tight isolated plate of the printed mark at native scale.

trajectory.action: Prepare the isolated raster for tracing: flatten what the printing process left behind so the trace receives an edge rather than a texture, inspecting at magnification first.
trajectory.judgement: The trace takes no options at all, so everything that will be true of the geometry has to be made true in the raster first. This is the only lever in the recovery.
trajectory.produces: A trace ready plate plus a note of what was flattened.

trajectory.action: Trace, then do the hygiene the tool does not: inject a real viewBox, remove the full canvas ground path, and place the result at the sizes it actually reproduces, reversed on the works green as well as positive.
trajectory.judgement: A trace judged at canvas size is not judged. The plate, the stamp and the bay door sign are three different questions and only one of them is flattering.
trajectory.produces: A first candidate master, judged at reproduction size on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Work the nameplate source on its own terms: isolate the etch by its own visual properties against brushed metal, invert, flatten to a plate, trace, hygiene it the same way.
trajectory.judgement: Etched metal has no ink, so wording that worked on printed board does not transfer, and one call background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring however convincing its output looks.
trajectory.produces: A second candidate master, comparable with the first.

trajectory.action: Choose the master and build the whole variant family off that ONE geometry: one colour, reversed knockout, full colour, and the single outline cut file.
trajectory.judgement: Separate traces would be faster and would drift within a season. Which lockup is current, with the place arc or without, is the client's history and cannot be inherited from whichever file traced better.
trajectory.produces: The master plus four derived variants sharing one geometry.

trajectory.action: Recover the works proving stamp from the struck test coupon on its own terms: isolate the die impression by its own near value properties against polished steel rather than by the coupon, separate the struck line from the burnished burr, keep the inspector's number box open, trace, hygiene it the same way, and judge it at the roughly nine millimetres it strikes into the plate corner reversed on the works green.
trajectory.judgement: Struck steel is a third medium again, neither ink pressed into board nor an etch cut out of brushed metal: the burr rings every stroke and reads as part of the mark, and the number box is empty in the die and must knock out rather than fill. A stamp judged at coupon scale is not judged, because it only ever goes small.
trajectory.produces: A recovered proving stamp as its own geometry, judged at strike size on the works green.

trajectory.action: Recover the 1919 cast heritage device from the raking light frame photograph: take the casting edge rather than the raking light shadow, since the badge is painted the works green over raised iron and the only edge signal is directional, discount the shallow draft ramp so the strokes do not double, trace and hygiene it, then assemble the three mark artwork system, one geometry family within each mark and no mark inheriting another's trace.
trajectory.judgement: The device is green on green, so a value threshold catches the shadow offset from the metal and returns an emblem shifted toward the lit side. It is a secondary mark that sits beside the company mark on the bay door and never carries the place arc, so it must be recovered as its own thing rather than lifted off the company mark because that one traced more easily.
trajectory.produces: A recovered heritage device plus the assembled three mark system, each mark its own geometry and its own variants.

trajectory.action: License a shop floor context frame at full resolution with short generic queries filtered to photography, then bring it, the cover, the nameplate frame and the levelled proving coupon and cast frame photographs to one works target and cut the transparent plate the usage sheet needs.
trajectory.judgement: Pick the frame whose light can be brought to the target rather than the best thumbnail. One batched move applies one identical correction, exactly wrong for five frames made under five different conditions.
trajectory.produces: A graded application set covering all five works photographs with a per frame parameter log, plus the transparent plate.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's plate PDF into a working layout, export its interchange form, and read what came back: the real frame inventory, the real story text, and how the plate's lines are distributed.
trajectory.judgement: The printed plate suggests six tidy fields. What the conversion produced is a different question, and it decides whether the mapping is per frame or position based inside one flow.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory and the document's own reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export the rebuilt document again and confirm every placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: Both the validator and the template builder report success on a mapping whose positions are wrong, so reading the rebuilt document is the only check that exists.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge the fourteen machines into one press file in order, then merge into the layout format and render a proof per machine at true plate resolution, checking identity by what is printed rather than by position.
trajectory.judgement: Position in a returned list is not identity and the labels on per record raster output are not evidence. Fourteen plates going to an engraver is where a swapped identity is found by the customer.
trajectory.produces: One fourteen page press file plus fourteen identified proofs at plate resolution.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a procurement engineer. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, so an assumed weight ships the wrong face silently.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the usage sheet, letterhead and stamp at true print canvases, the mark as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, the clear space guidance as drawn geometry, photography embedded as image data, family and weight per text element, then upload and export.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: The durable source HTML and a native editable document carrying all three canvases.

trajectory.action: Verify the export through the two channels that exist, the rendition for the first canvas and the returned markup for the rest, then build the shared board within the per call cap and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only shows the first artboard, so looking at the first canvas is not looking at the deliverable. A partial board placement is also reported as a success.
trajectory.produces: An audited export, a persistent board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the surviving source that looks best can actually yield production geometry. The 1974 cover was printed through a coarse screen, so once the ink is isolated the trace receives a field of dots rather than a line and returns lumpy stippled outlines that look correct at canvas size and read as a soft wobbling edge only at the size the mark reproduces, reversed on the works green. Nothing reports it: the trace takes no options at all, no threshold, no path count, no simplification, and its success message is identical whichever way it went.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it: the screen is a property of a 1974 printing, invisible in the file's name, dimensions and preview, legible only after the ink is isolated and traced. Nothing states it, since the client says only that this is the catalogue cover. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation entirely, or abandoning that source for the etched nameplate, a different medium needing a different isolation.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster for whichever source is now the candidate, re run the isolation with wording aimed at the mark, trace again, redo the hygiene, and judge again at reproduction size on the works green.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mark that opens cleanly, scales and looks right in the delivered folder, then reproduces as a soft dotty edge on the plate of a two hundred thousand dollar machine and on the bay door sign, which is what this buyer reads as sloppy engineering.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the works proving stamp survives at the size it is actually struck. It comes off the coupon as struck metal with no ink, so mark and polished ground sit at almost one value, and a raised burnished burr rings the whole impression. Whichever way the isolation goes it looks correct at coupon scale: take the burr and the glyph fattens, duck inside it and the thin ring rule and the number box outline thin away. The stamp does not go large anywhere; it strikes at about nine millimetres into the plate corner and prints small on the test certificate, and only at that size, reversed on the works green, does the burr fattened version close the bend angle apex and the ring counter into a blob while the number box the inspector must write into fills solid. The trace takes no options at all and its success message is identical whichever way it went.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it: the burr and the near equal value are properties of a die struck into steel, invisible in the file's name, dimensions and preview and legible only after the impression is isolated, traced and placed at nine millimetres on the green. Nothing states it, since the coupon is handed over as simply the stamp struck on a test offcut. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation entirely, separating the struck line from the burnished burr and deciding the number box before the trace rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the coupon raster to separate the struck line from the burr, re run the isolation aimed at the impression rather than the metal, keep the number box open, trace again, redo the hygiene, and judge again at nine millimetres reversed on the works green rather than at coupon scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A proving stamp that reads cleanly in the delivered folder, then strikes into the plate of a two hundred thousand dollar machine as a fattened blob with the inspector's number box filled solid, on the one device on the machine that is a load test record rather than branding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's plate PDF actually becomes once it is a working layout. Whether the plate's lines arrive as separately addressable blocks or as one continuous flow is a property of how the original was set rather than of how the printed plate looks, and it decides the entire mapping strategy. Worse, the readout of that text can omit a whole run while keeping the line break around it, so every position past the omission is short by exactly what was dropped, the validation still reports the mapping valid with no warnings, and the build still reports success while landing only some of the fields.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it: the granularity does not exist until the conversion has run, and the omission shows only against the document's own reconstructed text. Nothing states it, since the client says the layout is right and only the machine details change, which is true of the printed plate and silent about the file. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different mapping strategy built against a different source of truth.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document, recompute every position against it, rebuild the mapping in the form the real frame inventory supports, prepare again, and confirm each placeholder by reading the rebuilt document.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen plates that render, proof and print with two required fields silently absent, found by the engraver at best and a customer's inspector at worst, on a document that is part compliance record and part branding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every one of the fourteen machines fits the plate it was given. The model line is a fixed frame, and a fixed frame does not spill when it is overrun, it stops drawing: that page comes back looking finished with the designation cut at the frame edge, no overset warning, no error, no difference in the response, and the other thirteen pages perfectly correct. Which record does it, and whether it is one or three, is a property of how the order book reads this November against a measure that exists only inside the converted document.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is nothing to order around and nothing to get right first time: the frame measure only exists after the conversion and the strings only meet it at the merge. Nothing states it, since the client hands over the order book as it stands. It is not a propagation re run, because the fix is a decision about that record, abbreviate to the works naming rule, carry the suffix on the note line, or reset the field.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page against its source row rather than sampling, decide per affected record how the designation is carried against the client's naming rule, merge and render again, and re check all fourteen pages and the duplicate serial.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A machine ships carrying a plate with a truncated model designation, which on capital equipment is a compliance document as much as branding and is corrected by unbolting it.

deliverables.name: Recovered Redecker mark and its variant family
deliverables.spec: The 1919 lockup recovered from physical artefacts as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, counters and hairline rule open at reproduction size. One master plus a one colour version, a reversed knockout that genuinely opens on the works green, a full colour version, and a single closed outline file the laser house can cut, all off the same geometry. Beside it, two further marks recovered as their own geometry rather than as decorations lifted off the company mark: the works proving stamp, struck steel recovered so the bend angle apex, the ring counter and the inspector's open number box all survive at the roughly nine millimetres it strikes and reverse clean on the works green, with a one colour and a reversed knockout form; and the 1919 cast heritage device, recovered from the casting edge rather than the raking light shadow, carried as a secondary mark beside the company mark on the bay door sign with a closed outline cut form and never bearing the place arc. One system of three marks with one hygiene standard, each with its own viewBox and no mark a rescaled copy of another, not one mark at several sizes.

decision_gates: Which deliverables belong to a record per page run and which need an authored fixed canvas, since only one surface does each.
Which of the two surviving sources is the recovery source, judged on what each is physically made of rather than on which previews better.
Which lockup is the current mark, with the place arc or without, a decision about the company's history rather than about which file traced better.
How the isolation is worded on each source, since naming the object returns the board or the plate while naming the mark's own visual properties returns the mark, and both failures look successful.
Whether one call background removal is ever right on an enclosed ring, and what to use instead when the reversed variant is the deliverable.

Which isolation route recovers the struck proving stamp without carrying the burnished burr, and whether the inspector's number box is taken as an open knockout or silently filled solid, both of which look successful at coupon scale.

How the 1919 cast device's edge is taken, given the only edge signal is the raking light shadow rather than the metal, and whether that secondary device is current on the bay door and correctly carried without the place arc.
Whether the variant family comes off one geometry or off separate traces, invisible on delivery day and obvious in a year.
Whether the plate mapping is per frame or position based inside one flow, which the printed plate cannot tell you.
How the overlong designation is carried, which is the client's naming rule rather than the designer's preference, and whether the duplicate serial is a data error or two machines.
What to tell the client about what the pipeline cannot produce from their source file, including bleed, rather than quietly shipping without it.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome industrial logo. IDENTITY: this is one company's 1919 mark, still bolted to machines in customers' plants and stamped on decades of invoices, and a regenerated mark is a different company's logo however good it looks. The two surviving artefacts are the only evidence of what that mark is, and half the work is deciding which is admissible. And it is not one mark but three: ink on screened board and an etch in brushed steel for the company mark, a die struck into a steel coupon for the proving stamp, and a badge cast and painted into iron for the heritage device, four physical media that a generated picture is evidence of none of. SPEC: fourteen plates at one machine per page in order, each field present in full at trim, per machine proofs at plate resolution whose identity is confirmed by content, a closed path file a laser cutter can follow, and no interpolated pixels. None of that is satisfiable by a generated picture or checkable in one. EDITABILITY: the sign shop, the engraver, the printer and the laser house need real geometry rather than a picture of it, and the stationery is defined by the works being able to edit it next year.
doability_proof: Verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces honestly counted, image_vectorize counted as Photoshop family. No banned capability and no dead surface: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector (unretrievable headlessly), no animate_design, no fill_text, no upscaling, compositing, object removal, OCR, text to image, image to PDF, pdfPreset, variable QR, bleed gate from a PDF derived template, or batch above 20. IMAGING is verified headless across 27 live calls, and select, invert, crop to bounds, vectorize returns a real outline rather than a silhouette. Checkpoint one rests on verified findings: vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL so raster prep is the only lever; it emits NO viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path index zero; the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is verified at 154,926 pixels versus 9,372 on one image; and remove_background on an enclosed ring returns a solid opaque disc. The two additional mark recoveries add no new tool and no new surface: the struck proving stamp and the green on green cast device are isolated, prepared and traced with the same verified imaging calls (image_select_by_prompt, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_vectorize), and their failures are the same verified class, that vectorize takes no options so all recovery is raster preparation, that a near equal value ground and a burnished burr defeat a naive selection exactly as the etch does, and that the recovered geometry only reveals itself at the size and on the ground it actually reproduces. INDESIGN: convert, export_idml, mapping, prepare, merge and render are verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF output verified with page count equal to row count, per record files in correct order verified through createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop, and 300 DPI verified through document_render_layout. Checkpoint two rests on the verified textContent omission, where a dropped 17 character run left every later offset short while the validator reported VALID and the build reported success with only 3 of 5 mappings landing, plus the verified finding that PDF frame granularity is not under your control and can collapse to one frame. Checkpoint three rests on fixed frame behaviour in a converted press layout, with proof identity verified unsafe to infer from position because multi record raster URLs came back REVERSED while labelled in order. EXPRESS: true print canvases at exact millimetre resolution, inline SVG as native editable vector, mixed canvases in one export and an editable document findable by asset_search are verified, with the rendition documented as first canvas only. FONTS and STOCK AND BOARDS are verified end to end, including the kit case sensitivity trap, the non standard numeric weights, short Stock queries with orientation never passed, and boards persistent at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial.
